structural_breaks.note: Solar business (announced sale 2017-04-20) and Telvent DTN reclassified to discontinued operations; 2016 comparatives restated (Q1 2016 group 5,773 → 5,589; Q3 2016 6,064 → 6,015).
Businesses renamed Low Voltage (Building), Medium Voltage (Infrastructure), Secure Power (IT), Industrial Automation (Industry).
ASCO Power Technologies consolidated in Low Voltage (→ Energy Management).
Energy Management (MV+LV+Secure Power) and Industrial Automation presented; from Q1 2019 Energy Management reported as a single business (no MV split). AVEVA (IA) consolidated 2018-03-01.
Gutor disposal completed; Telemecanique Sensors disposal 2023-10-31; Schneider Electric Russia divestment agreed 2022-07-04.
Motivair (liquid cooling for data centers) acquisition completed — Energy Management/Secure Power.
Regions redefined (four regions) with re-cast 2023–2025 regional data; business split (EM/IA) unchanged.

profile.products: Energy Management: LV & MV power distribution (switchgear, switchboards, ring-main units, breakers — Square D in US), distribution transformers (not separately disclosed), Secure Power (UPS, cooling incl. Motivair liquid cooling, prefabricated data-center modules), building automation, EcoStruxure software/services, ETAP/RIB agnostic software. Q1 2026: Systems +16% led by data center; Power & Grid cited as strong end-market.

plants.products: new facility to grow medium-voltage presence / new MV products (2025–27 plan)
switchgear and power distribution products (campus expansion)
molded case and air circuit breakers
circuit breaker and related electrical products (2022 modernization)
customized switchgear for commercial buildings (per 2022 release)

profile.end_markets: Data Center & Networks (main growth driver 2023–26), Buildings (residential & commercial), Industry, Infrastructure incl. Power & Grid. North America ≈38% of Q1 2026 revenue; EM ≈82% of group revenue.
export_routes: FR/ES/IT->World (hypothesis, European MV/LV plants not verified here)

proxy_routes.why: US electrical equipment shipments — North America ≈38% of revenue, EM product sales
US electrical equipment new orders — leads EM systems revenue
Mexico ≤1 kV switchboard exports to US — Monterrey/Mexican plants supplying US (Square D)
US imports of LV boards from Mexico (mirror of MX->US route)
France >1 kV switchgear exports — Schneider French MV plants
French NACE C27.1 output — Schneider is a dominant French C27.1 producer
China LV board exports — China & East Asia hub
China grid investment — China & East Asia ≈18% of revenue
US power construction — Power & Grid end-market
US private data-center construction put-in-place (Census) — Data Center end-market driver; wishlist
